We start by rewriting the relation
\[
st=ts^3.
\]
Multiplying on the left by \(t\) gives
\[
tst=s^3,
\]
and then multiplying on the right by \(t\),
\[
ts=s^3t.
\]
Thus \(t\) acts on \(\langle s\rangle \cong C_8\) by
\[
s \mapsto s^3.
\]
Since \(3^2\equiv 1 \pmod 8\), this is an automorphism of order \(2\). Hence
\[
G\cong C_8\rtimes C_2,
\]
and every element has the form \(s^i\) or \(s^i t\), where \(i\in \mathbb Z/8\mathbb Z\). So \(|G|=16\).

We count conjugacy classes in the two cosets separately.

---

### 1. Conjugacy classes inside \(\langle s\rangle\)

Conjugation by powers of \(s\) fixes every element of \(\langle s\rangle\). Conjugation by \(t\) acts as
\[
t s^i t^{-1}=t s^i t=s^{3i}.
\]
So the conjugacy classes inside \(\langle s\rangle\) are the orbits of the map
\[
i\mapsto 3i \pmod 8.
\]

The orbits are:
\[
\{0\},\qquad \{1,3\},\qquad \{2,6\},\qquad \{4\},\qquad \{5,7\}.
\]
Thus \(\langle s\rangle\) contributes
\[
5
\]
conjugacy classes:
\[
\{1\},\quad \{s,s^3\},\quad \{s^2,s^6\},\quad \{s^4\},\quad \{s^5,s^7\}.
\]

---

### 2. Conjugacy classes in the coset \(s^i t\)

Let \(x_i=s^i t\). Conjugation by \(s\) gives
\[
s(s^i t)s^{-1}
=s^{i+1}ts^7
=s^{i+1}s^{21}t
=s^{i+1}s^5t
=s^{i+6}t
=s^{i-2}t.
\]
Thus conjugation by powers of \(s\) sends
\[
i\mapsto i-2k \pmod 8
\]
for some integer \(k\). Therefore it only changes \(i\) by an even amount, so parity is preserved, and all even indices are connected while all odd indices are connected.

Conjugation by \(t\) sends
\[
t(s^i t)t^{-1}=t(s^i t)t=t s^i=s^{3i}t,
\]
which also preserves parity. Hence the coset \(s^i t\) splits into exactly two conjugacy classes:

\[
\{t,s^2t,s^4t,s^6t\}
\]
and
\[
\{st,s^3t,s^5t,s^7t\}.
\]

So the coset contributes \(2\) conjugacy classes.

---

Therefore the total number of conjugacy classes of \(G\) is
\[
5+2=7.
\]

\[
\boxed{7}
\]
